The team's mascot is a black swallow with a red face named Tsubakuro (つば九郎, *Tsubakurō*). He is known for his feuds with the [Orix Buffaloes](/wiki/Orix_Buffaloes "Orix Buffaloes")' mascots. He always wears a batting helmet. Whenever the Swallows wear special home uniforms, Tsubakuro also wears the same.

The number on the back of his uniform is "2896" as opposed to 111/222 used by [Buffalo Bull and Buffalo Bell](/wiki/Orix_Buffaloes#Mascots "Orix Buffaloes"), the Buffaloes' mascots.

There is also a female swallow mascot named Tsubami. She wears a skirt and may be intended as Tsubakuro's little sister, just as Bell is Bull's little sister. Unlike her brother, she wears a sports visor.

Before Tsubakuro was created, the team's mascots were Yabo (ヤー坊, *Yābō*) and Sue-chan (スーちゃん, *Sū-chan*), who were the team mascots from 1979 to 1994.

The team also had a third mascot named Torcuya (トルクーヤ, *Torukūya*), a swallow who resembles a [luchador](/wiki/Luchador "Luchador"). He always carries around a parasol and a bottle of Yakult that he carries on his back.

The team also had a former mascot named Entaro (燕太郎, *Entarō*), a swallow who wore a jersey with the number 8960. He was replaced by Torcuya in 2014.

The Swallows farm team plays in the [Eastern League](/wiki/Eastern_League_(Japanese_baseball) "Eastern League (Japanese baseball)"). The team was founded in 1950.

The period between 1900 and 1919 is commonly referred to as the "dead-ball era".[[20]](#cite_note-:4-20) Games of this era tended to be low-scoring and were often dominated by pitchers, such as [Walter Johnson](/wiki/Walter_Johnson "Walter Johnson"), [Cy Young](/wiki/Cy_Young "Cy Young"), [Christy Mathewson](/wiki/Christy_Mathewson "Christy Mathewson"), [Mordecai Brown](/wiki/Mordecai_Brown "Mordecai Brown"), and [Grover Cleveland Alexander](/wiki/Grover_Cleveland_Alexander "Grover Cleveland Alexander"). The term also accurately describes the condition of the baseball itself. The baseball used American rather than the modern Australian wool yarn and was not wound as tightly, affecting the distance that it would travel.[[42]](#cite_note-McNeil-42) More significantly, balls were kept in play until they were mangled, soft and sometimes lopsided. During this era, a baseball cost $3,[[43]](#cite_note-43) (equivalent to $56 in 2025), and owners were reluctant to purchase new balls. Fans were expected to throw back fouls and (rare) home runs. Baseballs also became stained with tobacco juice, grass, and mud, and sometimes the juice of licorice, which some players would chew for the purpose of discoloring the ball.[[44]](#cite_note-Keating-44)

AlphaGo's victory was a major milestone in artificial intelligence research.[[69]](#cite_note-latimes_milestone-69) Go had previously been regarded as a hard problem in machine learning that was expected to be out of reach for the technology of the time.[[69]](#cite_note-latimes_milestone-69)[[70]](#cite_note-70)[[71]](#cite_note-71) Most experts thought a Go program as powerful as AlphaGo was at least five years away;[[72]](#cite_note-72) some experts thought that it would take at least another decade before computers would beat Go champions.[[73]](#cite_note-cbc_sweeps-73)[[74]](#cite_note-74) Most observers at the beginning of the 2016 matches expected Lee to beat AlphaGo.[[69]](#cite_note-latimes_milestone-69)

With games such as checkers, chess, and now Go won by computer players, victories at popular board games can no longer serve as significant milestones for artificial intelligence in the way that they used to. [Deep Blue](/wiki/Deep_Blue_(chess_computer) "Deep Blue (chess computer)")'s [Murray Campbell](/wiki/Murray_Campbell "Murray Campbell") called AlphaGo's victory "the end of an era... board games are more or less done and it's time to move on."[[69]](#cite_note-latimes_milestone-69)

When compared with Deep Blue or with [Watson](/wiki/Watson_(computer) "Watson (computer)"), AlphaGo's underlying algorithms are potentially more general-purpose and may be evidence that the scientific community is making progress toward [artificial general intelligence](/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence "Artificial general intelligence").[[75]](#cite_note-75) Some commentators believe AlphaGo's victory makes for a good opportunity for society to start discussing preparations for the possible future impact of [machines with general purpose intelligence](/wiki/Artificial_general_intelligence "Artificial general intelligence").
